    91	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    93	-/
    94	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    95	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    96	
    97	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   101	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   102	
   103	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   105	-/
   106	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   107	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   108	
   109	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   110	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   111	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   112	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   115	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   116	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   117	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   118	
   119	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   121	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   122	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   124	-/
   125	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   126	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   127	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   128	
   129	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   130	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   131	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   133	-/
   134	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   135	  fun i => match i with
   136	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   137	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   138	  | .inr _ => 0
   139	
   140	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   141	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   142	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   143	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   144	-/
   145	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   146	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   147	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   148	  fun i => match i with
   149	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   150	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   151	  | .inr _ => 0
   152	
   153	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   154	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   155	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   163	  fun i => match i with
   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j
   167	
   168	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   169	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   170	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   172	-/
   173	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   174	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   175	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   176	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   177	
   178	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar
   179	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the
   180	concatenation exhibiting the conditional-linearity levels asserted in
   181	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   182	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   183	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   184	private def ldSeedRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=

   187	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the point coordinates
   188	of the ambient low-degree space; see `ldSeedRegister`. -/
   189	private def ldPointRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=

   189	private theorem map_uniformDistribution_chiIndex (L : LdParams) :
   190	    (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)).map (chiIndex L) =
   191	      uniformDistribution (Fin L.m) :=
   192	  uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (L.q / L.m) (card_chiIndex_fiber L)
   193	
   194	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: zeroing an initial segment of the
   195	coordinates is idempotent. -/
   196	private theorem prefixProjection_prefixProjection (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m)
   197	    (v : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :
   198	    prefixProjection i (prefixProjection i v) = prefixProjection i v := by
   199	  funext j
   200	  by_cases h : j.val < i.val
   201	  · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h]
   202	  · simp only [prefixProjection, if_neg h]

   204	/-- `lem:alnf`: the point and axis-index marginals of the axis line-point
   205	distribution are uniform. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:101-106`, paper
   206	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`. -/
   207	theorem aLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform (L : LdParams) :
   208	    (aLinePointDist L).map Prod.snd =
   209	        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) ∧
   210	      (aLinePointDist L).map (fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed) =
   211	        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m) := by
   212	  constructor
   213	  · have hmap : (aLinePointDist L).map Prod.snd
   214	        = (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point := by
   215	      change ((((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   216	          fun z => (ldALineCL L z, ldPointCL L z)).map
   217	          fun s => (aLineDescOf L s.1, LdSpace.point s.2)).map Prod.snd) = _
   218	      rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
   219	      rfl
   220	    rw [hmap, map_uniformDistribution_point]
   221	  · have hmap : (aLinePointDist L).map (fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed)
   222	        = ((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.seed).map (chiIndex L) := by
   223	      change ((((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   224	          fun z => (ldALineCL L z, ldPointCL L z)).map
   225	          fun s => (aLineDescOf L s.1, LdSpace.point s.2)).map
   226	          fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed) = _
   227	      rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
   228	      rfl
   229	    rw [hmap, map_uniformDistribution_seed, map_uniformDistribution_chiIndex]

   231	/-- The incidence conclusion of `lem:alnf`, blueprint
   232	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:101-106`, paper
   233	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`. -/
   234	theorem aLinePointDist_mem_line (L : LdParams) :
   235	    ∀ sample ∈ (aLinePointDist L).support, sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
   236	  intro sample hsample
   237	  have hsupport : (aLinePointDist L).support =
   238	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (LdSpace L)).image
   239	        fun z => (ldALineCL L z, ldPointCL L z)).image
   240	        fun s => (aLineDescOf L s.1, LdSpace.point s.2) := rfl
   241	  rw [hsupport] at hsample
   242	  obtain ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hsample
   243	  obtain ⟨z, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
   244	  change LdSpace.point z ∈
   245	    linePoints
   246	      (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)))
   247	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)))
   248	          (LdSpace.point z)))
   249	      (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)))
   250	  rw [lineRepMap_apply_self]
   251	  exact mem_linePoints_lineRepMap _ _

   253	/-- `lem:dlnf`: the point and prefix-index marginals of the diagonal

   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
+vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
+private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
+    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
+  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
+  invFun p := fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
+    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
+    | .inr j => p.2 j
+  left_inv z := by
+    funext i
+    rcases i with (j | u) | j
+    · rfl
+    · cases u
+      rfl
+    · rfl
+  right_inv p := by
+    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
+    rfl

+  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =

+    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
+          rw [uniformDistribution_map_fst]

     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Marginals of finite distributions
     5	
     6	Shared push-forward lemmas for the project's finite `Distribution` type:
     7	extensionality through the associated probability mass function, composition
     8	of push-forwards, and the uniform first marginal of the uniform law on an
     9	explicit finite product.  They serve the marginal statements `lem:alnf` and
    10	`lem:dlnf` of the low-degree line-point laws and the question-law transport
    11	between the seed-indexed and directly indexed low-degree games.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`
    16	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	
    25	/-- Two probabilistic finite distributions with the same stored support and
    26	the same associated probability mass function are equal. -/
    27	theorem distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq {alpha : Type*}
    28	    (mu nu : Distribution alpha) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    29	    (hnu : nu.IsProbability) (hsupport : mu.support = nu.support)
    30	    (hpmf : mu.toPMF hmu = nu.toPMF hnu) : mu = nu := by
    31	  have hweight : mu.weight = nu.weight := by
    32	    funext a
    33	    calc
    34	      mu.weight a = (mu.toPMF hmu a).toReal :=
    35	        (Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal mu hmu a).symm
    36	      _ = (nu.toPMF hnu a).toReal := by rw [hpmf]
    37	      _ = nu.weight a := Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal nu hnu a
    38	  cases mu with
    39	  | mk muSupport muWeight muNonnegative muOutsideSupport =>
    40	      cases nu with
    41	      | mk nuSupport nuWeight nuNonnegative nuOutsideSupport =>
    42	          cases hsupport
    43	          cases hweight
    44	          rfl
    45	
    46	/-- Composition of two push-forwards of a probabilistic finite distribution
    47	is the push-forward by the composite map. -/
    48	theorem distribution_map_map_of_isProbability
    49	    {alpha beta gamma : Type*} [DecidableEq beta] [DecidableEq gamma]
    50	    (mu : Distribution alpha) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    51	    (f : alpha → beta) (g : beta → gamma) :
    52	    (mu.map f).map g = mu.map (g ∘ f) := by
    53	  apply distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq
    54	    ((mu.map f).map g) (mu.map (g ∘ f))
    55	    ((hmu.map f).map g) (hmu.map (g ∘ f))
    56	  · simp [Distribution.map_support, Finset.image_image]
    57	  · calc
    58	      ((mu.map f).map g).toPMF ((hmu.map f).map g) =
    59	          ((mu.map f).toPMF (hmu.map f)).map g :=
    60	        Distribution.toPMF_map (mu.map f) (hmu.map f) g
    61	      _ = ((mu.toPMF hmu).map f).map g := by
    62	        rw [Distribution.toPMF_map mu hmu f]
    63	      _ = (mu.toPMF hmu).map (g ∘ f) :=
    64	        PMF.map_comp f (mu.toPMF hmu) g
    65	      _ = (mu.map (g ∘ f)).toPMF (hmu.map (g ∘ f)) :=
    66	        (Distribution.toPMF_map mu hmu (g ∘ f)).symm
    67	
    68	/-- Projection onto the first factor of an explicit finite product
    69	equivalence sends the uniform distribution to the uniform first marginal. -/
    70	theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
    71	    {alpha beta gamma : Type*}
    72	    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha] [Nonempty alpha]
    73	    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta] [Nonempty beta]
    74	    [Finite gamma] [Nonempty gamma]
    75	    (e : alpha ≃ beta × gamma) (f : alpha → beta)
    76	    (hf : ∀ a, f a = (e a).1) :
    77	    (uniformDistribution alpha).map f = uniformDistribution beta := by
    78	  classical
    79	  letI : Fintype gamma := Fintype.ofFinite gamma
    80	  have hsurjective : Function.Surjective f := by
    81	    intro b
    82	    let c : gamma := Classical.choice (inferInstance : Nonempty gamma)
    83	    refine ⟨e.symm (b, c), ?_⟩
    84	    simpa using hf (e.symm (b, c))
    85	  apply distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq

/-!
# Marginals of finite distributions

Shared push-forward lemmas for the project's finite `Distribution` type:
extensionality through the associated probability mass function, composition
of push-forwards, and the uniform first marginal of the uniform law on an
explicit finite product.  They serve the marginal statements `lem:alnf` and
`lem:dlnf` of the low-degree line-point laws and the question-law transport
between the seed-indexed and directly indexed low-degree games.

## References

- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`
- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- Two probabilistic finite distributions with the same stored support and
the same associated probability mass function are equal. -/
theorem distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq {alpha : Type*}
    (mu nu : Distribution alpha) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    (hnu : nu.IsProbability) (hsupport : mu.support = nu.support)
    (hpmf : mu.toPMF hmu = nu.toPMF hnu) : mu = nu := by
  have hweight : mu.weight = nu.weight := by
    funext a
    calc
      mu.weight a = (mu.toPMF hmu a).toReal :=
        (Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal mu hmu a).symm
      _ = (nu.toPMF hnu a).toReal := by rw [hpmf]
      _ = nu.weight a := Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal nu hnu a
  cases mu with
  | mk muSupport muWeight muNonnegative muOutsideSupport =>
      cases nu with
      | mk nuSupport nuWeight nuNonnegative nuOutsideSupport =>
          cases hsupport
          cases hweight
          rfl

/-- Composition of two push-forwards of a probabilistic finite distribution
is the push-forward by the composite map. -/
theorem distribution_map_map_of_isProbability
    {alpha beta gamma : Type*} [DecidableEq beta] [DecidableEq gamma]
    (mu : Distribution alpha) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    (f : alpha → beta) (g : beta → gamma) :
    (mu.map f).map g = mu.map (g ∘ f) := by
  apply distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq
    ((mu.map f).map g) (mu.map (g ∘ f))
    ((hmu.map f).map g) (hmu.map (g ∘ f))
  · simp [Distribution.map_support, Finset.image_image]
  · calc
      ((mu.map f).map g).toPMF ((hmu.map f).map g) =
          ((mu.map f).toPMF (hmu.map f)).map g :=
        Distribution.toPMF_map (mu.map f) (hmu.map f) g
      _ = ((mu.toPMF hmu).map f).map g := by
        rw [Distribution.toPMF_map mu hmu f]
      _ = (mu.toPMF hmu).map (g ∘ f) :=
        PMF.map_comp f (mu.toPMF hmu) g
      _ = (mu.map (g ∘ f)).toPMF (hmu.map (g ∘ f)) :=
        (Distribution.toPMF_map mu hmu (g ∘ f)).symm

/-- Projection onto the first factor of an explicit finite product
equivalence sends the uniform distribution to the uniform first marginal. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
    {alpha beta gamma : Type*}
    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha] [Nonempty alpha]
    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta] [Nonempty beta]
    [Finite gamma] [Nonempty gamma]
    (e : alpha ≃ beta × gamma) (f : alpha → beta)
    (hf : ∀ a, f a = (e a).1) :
    (uniformDistribution alpha).map f = uniformDistribution beta := by
  classical
  letI : Fintype gamma := Fintype.ofFinite gamma
  have hsurjective : Function.Surjective f := by
    intro b
    let c : gamma := Classical.choice (inferInstance : Nonempty gamma)
    refine ⟨e.symm (b, c), ?_⟩
    simpa using hf (e.symm (b, c))
  apply distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq
    ((uniformDistribution alpha).map f) (uniformDistribution beta)
    ((uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha).map f)
    (uniformDistribution_isProbability beta)
  · rw [Distribution.map_support, uniformDistribution_support,
      uniformDistribution_support,
      Finset.image_univ_of_surjective hsurjective]
  · calc
      ((uniformDistribution alpha).map f).toPMF
          ((uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha).map f) =
          ((uniformDistribution alpha).toPMF
            (uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha)).map f :=
        Distribution.toPMF_map (uniformDistribution alpha)
          (uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha) f
      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map f := by
        rw [uniformDistribution_toPMF]
      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map
          (Prod.fst ∘ e) := by
            exact congrArg
              (fun map : alpha → beta => (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map map)
              (funext fun a => by simpa [Function.comp_def] using hf a)
      _ = ((PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map e).map Prod.fst :=
        (PMF.map_comp e (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha) Prod.fst).symm
      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype (beta × gamma)).map Prod.fst := by
        rw [PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv e]
      _ = PMF.uniformOfFintype beta := by
        rw [PMF.uniformOfFintype_prod_eq_bind]
        calc
          ((PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind fun a =>
              (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map Prod.fst =
              (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind (fun a =>
                ((PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map
                  Prod.fst) :=
            PMF.map_bind (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta)
              (fun a => (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b))
              Prod.fst
          _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind (fun a => PMF.pure a) := by
            apply congrArg (fun q : beta → PMF beta =>
              (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind q)
            funext a
            calc
              ((PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map
                  Prod.fst =
                  (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map
                    (Prod.fst ∘ fun b => (a, b)) :=
                PMF.map_comp _ (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma) Prod.fst
              _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map
                  (Function.const gamma a) := by rfl
              _ = PMF.pure a :=
                PMF.map_const (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma) a
          _ = PMF.uniformOfFintype beta :=
            PMF.bind_pure (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta)
      _ = (uniformDistribution beta).toPMF
          (uniformDistribution_isProbability beta) :=
        (uniformDistribution_toPMF beta).symm

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.PMFAverages
+
+/-!
+# Marginals of finite distributions
+
+Shared push-forward lemmas for the project's finite `Distribution` type:
+extensionality through the associated probability mass function, composition
+of push-forwards, and the uniform first marginal of the uniform law on an
+explicit finite product.  They serve the marginal statements `lem:alnf` and
+`lem:dlnf` of the low-degree line-point laws and the question-law transport
+between the seed-indexed and directly indexed low-degree games.
+
+## References
+
+- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`
+- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+
+/-- Two probabilistic finite distributions with the same stored support and
+the same associated probability mass function are equal. -/
+theorem distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq {alpha : Type*}
+    (mu nu : Distribution alpha) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
+    (hnu : nu.IsProbability) (hsupport : mu.support = nu.support)
+    (hpmf : mu.toPMF hmu = nu.toPMF hnu) : mu = nu := by
+  have hweight : mu.weight = nu.weight := by
+    funext a
+    calc
+      mu.weight a = (mu.toPMF hmu a).toReal :=
+        (Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal mu hmu a).symm
+      _ = (nu.toPMF hnu a).toReal := by rw [hpmf]
+      _ = nu.weight a := Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal nu hnu a
+  cases mu with
+  | mk muSupport muWeight muNonnegative muOutsideSupport =>
+      cases nu with
+      | mk nuSupport nuWeight nuNonnegative nuOutsideSupport =>
+          cases hsupport
+          cases hweight
+          rfl
+
+/-- Composition of two push-forwards of a probabilistic finite distribution
+is the push-forward by the composite map. -/
+theorem distribution_map_map_of_isProbability
+    {alpha beta gamma : Type*} [DecidableEq beta] [DecidableEq gamma]
+    (mu : Distribution alpha) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
+    (f : alpha → beta) (g : beta → gamma) :
+    (mu.map f).map g = mu.map (g ∘ f) := by
+  apply distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq
+    ((mu.map f).map g) (mu.map (g ∘ f))
+    ((hmu.map f).map g) (hmu.map (g ∘ f))
+  · simp [Distribution.map_support, Finset.image_image]
+  · calc
+      ((mu.map f).map g).toPMF ((hmu.map f).map g) =
+          ((mu.map f).toPMF (hmu.map f)).map g :=
+        Distribution.toPMF_map (mu.map f) (hmu.map f) g
+      _ = ((mu.toPMF hmu).map f).map g := by
+        rw [Distribution.toPMF_map mu hmu f]
+      _ = (mu.toPMF hmu).map (g ∘ f) :=
+        PMF.map_comp f (mu.toPMF hmu) g
+      _ = (mu.map (g ∘ f)).toPMF (hmu.map (g ∘ f)) :=
+        (Distribution.toPMF_map mu hmu (g ∘ f)).symm
+
+/-- Projection onto the first factor of an explicit finite product
+equivalence sends the uniform distribution to the uniform first marginal. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
+    {alpha beta gamma : Type*}
+    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha] [Nonempty alpha]
+    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta] [Nonempty beta]
+    [Finite gamma] [Nonempty gamma]
+    (e : alpha ≃ beta × gamma) (f : alpha → beta)
+    (hf : ∀ a, f a = (e a).1) :
+    (uniformDistribution alpha).map f = uniformDistribution beta := by
+  classical
+  letI : Fintype gamma := Fintype.ofFinite gamma
+  have hsurjective : Function.Surjective f := by
+    intro b
+    let c : gamma := Classical.choice (inferInstance : Nonempty gamma)
+    refine ⟨e.symm (b, c), ?_⟩
+    simpa using hf (e.symm (b, c))
+  apply distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq
+    ((uniformDistribution alpha).map f) (uniformDistribution beta)
+    ((uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha).map f)
+    (uniformDistribution_isProbability beta)
+  · rw [Distribution.map_support, uniformDistribution_support,
+      uniformDistribution_support,
+      Finset.image_univ_of_surjective hsurjective]
+  · calc
+      ((uniformDistribution alpha).map f).toPMF
+          ((uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha).map f) =
+          ((uniformDistribution alpha).toPMF
+            (uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha)).map f :=
+        Distribution.toPMF_map (uniformDistribution alpha)
+          (uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha) f
+      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map f := by
+        rw [uniformDistribution_toPMF]
+      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map
+          (Prod.fst ∘ e) := by
+            exact congrArg
+              (fun map : alpha → beta => (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map map)
+              (funext fun a => by simpa [Function.comp_def] using hf a)
+      _ = ((PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map e).map Prod.fst :=
+        (PMF.map_comp e (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha) Prod.fst).symm
+      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype (beta × gamma)).map Prod.fst := by
+        rw [PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv e]
+      _ = PMF.uniformOfFintype beta := by
+        rw [PMF.uniformOfFintype_prod_eq_bind]
+        calc
+          ((PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind fun a =>
+              (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map Prod.fst =
+              (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind (fun a =>
+                ((PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map
+                  Prod.fst) :=
+            PMF.map_bind (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta)
+              (fun a => (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b))
+              Prod.fst
+          _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind (fun a => PMF.pure a) := by
+            apply congrArg (fun q : beta → PMF beta =>
+              (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind q)
+            funext a
+            calc
+              ((PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map
+                  Prod.fst =
+                  (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map
+                    (Prod.fst ∘ fun b => (a, b)) :=
+                PMF.map_comp _ (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma) Prod.fst
+              _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map
+                  (Function.const gamma a) := by rfl
+              _ = PMF.pure a :=
+                PMF.map_const (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma) a
+          _ = PMF.uniformOfFintype beta :=
+            PMF.bind_pure (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta)
+      _ = (uniformDistribution beta).toPMF
+          (uniformDistribution_isProbability beta) :=
+        (uniformDistribution_toPMF beta).symm
+

   182	The proof uses the intrinsic prefix-rank characterization; equivalence with a

   185	theorem isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement {n : ℕ}

   229	    ext k

     3	/-!
     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and
     8	provides the canonical projection used for line representatives.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-520`;
    14	the formalization support nodes `lem:line-rep-kernel` and
    15	`lem:line-rep-incidence` are at `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:522-550`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators
    22	
    23	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    24	
    25	/--
    26	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    27	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`;
    28	paper origin
    29	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    30	-/
    31	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    32	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    33	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    34	
    35	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    36	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`, paper origin
    37	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    38	-/
    39	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    40	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    41	  Pi.single i 1
    42	
    43	/--
    44	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    45	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 464-478; paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    47	-/
    48	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    49	  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i
    50	
    51	/--
    52	The diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may
    53	vanish.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`; paper origin
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    55	-/
    56	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    57	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0
    58	
    59	/--
    60	Changing the base point to another point on a line leaves the line unchanged.
    61	This is `prop:line-equiv` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:480-486`,
    62	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:128-132`.
    63	-/
    64	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}
    65	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :
    66	    linePoints u v = linePoints u' v := by
    67	  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := h
    68	  ext x
    69	  constructor
    70	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    71	    exact ⟨s - t, by module⟩
    72	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    73	    exact ⟨t + s, by module⟩
    74	
    75	/--
    76	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    77	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,
    78	so the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`,
    79	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:500-520`; paper origin
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    81	-/
    82	noncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}
    83	    (v : Fin m → K) : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K) :=
    84	  canonicalProjOfKernel (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))
    85	
    86	/- The point-valued companion to `lineRepMap`; Lean-only notation for the
    87	canonical representative in `def:line-representative`. -/
    88	/-- The canonical representative point `lineRepMap v u`.  Blueprint
    89	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:500-520`, paper origin
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:166-174`.
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def lineRep {m : ℕ}
    93	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Fin m → K :=
    94	  lineRepMap v u
    95	
    96	/--
    97	Formalization support node `lem:line-rep-kernel` for
    98	`def:line-representative` (blueprint
    99	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:522-530`, paper origin
   100	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`).
   101	The canonical representative map is a projection whose kernel is the line
   102	`K v`, so a point and its canonical representative differ by a scalar multiple
   103	of the direction.
   104	-/
   105	theorem sub_lineRepMap_mem_span {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
   106	    u - lineRepMap v u ∈ Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)) := by
   107	  have hc :
   108	      IsCompl
   109	        (registerSubmodule K
   110	          (canonicalComplement (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))))
   111	        (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))) :=
   112	    (isCompl_registerSubmodule_canonicalComplement
   113	      (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))).symm
   114	  have hrep : lineRepMap v u =
   115	      (registerSubmodule K
   116	        (canonicalComplement (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))))).projection
   117	        (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K))) hc u := rfl
   118	  rw [hrep, ← Submodule.projection_eq_self_sub_projection hc u]
   119	  exact Submodule.projection_apply_mem hc.symm u
   120	
   121	/--
   122	Formalization support node `lem:line-rep-incidence` for
   123	`def:line-representative` (blueprint
   124	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:537-545`, paper origin
   125	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:166-174`).
   126	Every point lies on the line through its own canonical representative in the
   127	same direction; this is the incidence property used by the line-versus-point
   128	samplers.
   129	-/
   130	theorem mem_linePoints_lineRepMap {m : ℕ} (v u : Fin m → K) :
   131	    u ∈ linePoints (lineRepMap v u) v := by
   132	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp (sub_lineRepMap_mem_span v u)
   133	  exact ⟨t, by rw [ht]; abel⟩
   134	
   135	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+# Coordinate direct sums of conditionally linear representations
+
+This module assembles the direct sum of equal-level representations of
+conditionally linear functions over a family of pairwise disjoint registers,
+together with the coordinate-restriction lemmas its support and evaluation
+proofs rely on.  It is the supporting layer of
+`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/CondLinearTheorems.lean`, the module that owns the
+behaviour of conditionally linear maps and of their shared-seed distributions

+/-- A representation of a conditionally linear function supported on a register
+takes values that vanish off that register.  This is a formalization-only
+auxiliary for `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint `lem:cl-supported-vanishing`. -/
+theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t x a = 0 := by
+  induction t generalizing S with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
+      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
+      change (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
+        CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x) a = 0
+      rw [Pi.add_apply, hSupport _ a (fun haS₁ => ha (hS₁ haS₁))]
+      rw [ih _ (hrest _) (fun haDiff => ha (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp haDiff).1)]
+      exact zero_add 0

+/-- A supported representation of a conditionally linear function depends only
+on the coordinates in its register. -/
+private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_congr_of_eq_on {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) {x y : ι → K}
+    (hxy : ∀ a ∈ S, x a = y a) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t x = CondLinearTerm.eval t y := by
+  induction t generalizing S with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
+      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
+      have hrestrict : coordinateRestriction S₁ x = coordinateRestriction S₁ y := by
+        ext a
+        by_cases ha : a ∈ S₁
+        · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hxy a (hS₁ ha)]
+        · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]

+function does not change its value.  This is a formalization-only auxiliary
+for `lem:cl-func-prod` and `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint

+theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
+    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
+    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (x : ι → K) :
+    CondLinearTerm.eval t (coordinateRestriction S x) = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
+  exact CondLinearTerm.eval_congr_of_eq_on ht fun a ha => by

+restriction to a smaller register.  This is a formalization-only auxiliary
+for `lem:cl-kth` and `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint

+theorem coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [DecidableEq ι] {S T : Finset ι} (hST : S ⊆ T) (x : ι → K) :
+    coordinateRestriction S (coordinateRestriction T x) = coordinateRestriction S x := by
+  ext a
+  by_cases ha : a ∈ S
+  · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hST ha]
+  · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]
+
+/-- In a register partition, restricting a sum of supported vectors selects

+`lem:cl-func-prod` and `lem:cl-dist-prod`, blueprint

+theorem coordinateRestriction_sum_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
+    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
+    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
+    (f : J → ι → K) (hf : ∀ j a, a ∉ V j → f j a = 0) (j : J) :
+    coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, f i) = f j := by
+  ext a
+  by_cases ha : a ∈ V j
+  · rw [coordinateRestriction]
+    simp only [ha, ↓reduceIte, Finset.sum_apply]
+    apply Finset.sum_eq_single j

+      exact Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai ha
+    · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
+  · rw [coordinateRestriction]

+private def CondLinearTerm.headSupport {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} :

+    CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))

+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}

+  cases t with

+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}

+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.
    63	\end{definition}
    64	
    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}
    83	
    84	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear distributions]
    85	  Let $\type$ be a type set and
    86	  $L=\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type},R=\{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$ be $\type$-typed
    87	  families of conditionally linear functions on~$V$.
    88	  Let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph with vertex set $\type$.
    89	  The \emph{$(\type, G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,\,
    90	      R}^G$ corresponding to~$(L, R)$} is the distribution over pairs $( (\lvar,
    91	  x), (\rvar, y) )$, where $(\lvar, \rvar)$ is drawn from $\mu_G$ and $(x,y)$ is
    92	  drawn from $\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    93	\end{definition}

/-!
# Marginals of finite distributions

Shared push-forward lemmas for the project's finite `Distribution` type:
extensionality through the associated probability mass function, composition
of push-forwards, and the uniform first marginal of the uniform law on an
explicit finite product.  They serve the marginal statements `lem:alnf` and
`lem:dlnf` of the low-degree line-point laws and the question-law transport
between the seed-indexed and directly indexed low-degree games.

## References

- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`
- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
-/

/-- Two probabilistic finite distributions with the same stored support and
the same associated probability mass function are equal. -/
theorem distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq {alpha : Type*}
    (mu nu : Distribution alpha) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    (hnu : nu.IsProbability) (hsupport : mu.support = nu.support)
    (hpmf : mu.toPMF hmu = nu.toPMF hnu) : mu = nu := by
  have hweight : mu.weight = nu.weight := by
    funext a
    calc
      mu.weight a = (mu.toPMF hmu a).toReal :=
        (Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal mu hmu a).symm
      _ = (nu.toPMF hnu a).toReal := by rw [hpmf]
      _ = nu.weight a := Distribution.toPMF_apply_toReal nu hnu a
  cases mu with
  | mk muSupport muWeight muNonnegative muOutsideSupport =>
      cases nu with
      | mk nuSupport nuWeight nuNonnegative nuOutsideSupport =>
          cases hsupport
          cases hweight
          rfl

/-- Composition of two push-forwards of a probabilistic finite distribution
is the push-forward by the composite map. -/
theorem distribution_map_map_of_isProbability
    {alpha beta gamma : Type*} [DecidableEq beta] [DecidableEq gamma]
    (mu : Distribution alpha) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    (f : alpha → beta) (g : beta → gamma) :
    (mu.map f).map g = mu.map (g ∘ f) := by
  apply distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq
    ((mu.map f).map g) (mu.map (g ∘ f))
    ((hmu.map f).map g) (hmu.map (g ∘ f))
  · simp [Distribution.map_support, Finset.image_image]
  · calc
      ((mu.map f).map g).toPMF ((hmu.map f).map g) =
          ((mu.map f).toPMF (hmu.map f)).map g :=
        Distribution.toPMF_map (mu.map f) (hmu.map f) g
      _ = ((mu.toPMF hmu).map f).map g := by
        rw [Distribution.toPMF_map mu hmu f]
      _ = (mu.toPMF hmu).map (g ∘ f) :=
        PMF.map_comp f (mu.toPMF hmu) g
      _ = (mu.map (g ∘ f)).toPMF (hmu.map (g ∘ f)) :=
        (Distribution.toPMF_map mu hmu (g ∘ f)).symm

/-- Projection onto the first factor of an explicit finite product
equivalence sends the uniform distribution to the uniform first marginal. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv
    {alpha beta gamma : Type*}
    [Fintype alpha] [DecidableEq alpha] [Nonempty alpha]
    [Fintype beta] [DecidableEq beta] [Nonempty beta]
    [Finite gamma] [Nonempty gamma]
    (e : alpha ≃ beta × gamma) (f : alpha → beta)
    (hf : ∀ a, f a = (e a).1) :
    (uniformDistribution alpha).map f = uniformDistribution beta := by
  classical
  letI : Fintype gamma := Fintype.ofFinite gamma
  have hsurjective : Function.Surjective f := by
    intro b
    let c : gamma := Classical.choice (inferInstance : Nonempty gamma)
    refine ⟨e.symm (b, c), ?_⟩
    simpa using hf (e.symm (b, c))
  apply distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq
    ((uniformDistribution alpha).map f) (uniformDistribution beta)
    ((uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha).map f)
    (uniformDistribution_isProbability beta)
  · rw [Distribution.map_support, uniformDistribution_support,
      uniformDistribution_support,
      Finset.image_univ_of_surjective hsurjective]
  · calc
      ((uniformDistribution alpha).map f).toPMF
          ((uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha).map f) =
          ((uniformDistribution alpha).toPMF
            (uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha)).map f :=
        Distribution.toPMF_map (uniformDistribution alpha)
          (uniformDistribution_isProbability alpha) f
      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map f := by
        rw [uniformDistribution_toPMF]
      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map
          (Prod.fst ∘ e) := by
            exact congrArg
              (fun map : alpha → beta => (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map map)
              (funext fun a => by simpa [Function.comp_def] using hf a)
      _ = ((PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha).map e).map Prod.fst :=
        (PMF.map_comp e (PMF.uniformOfFintype alpha) Prod.fst).symm
      _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype (beta × gamma)).map Prod.fst := by
        rw [PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv e]
      _ = PMF.uniformOfFintype beta := by
        rw [PMF.uniformOfFintype_prod_eq_bind]
        calc
          ((PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind fun a =>
              (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map Prod.fst =
              (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind (fun a =>
                ((PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map
                  Prod.fst) :=
            PMF.map_bind (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta)
              (fun a => (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b))
              Prod.fst
          _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind (fun a => PMF.pure a) := by
            apply congrArg (fun q : beta → PMF beta =>
              (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta).bind q)
            funext a
            calc
              ((PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map fun b => (a, b)).map
                  Prod.fst =
                  (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map
                    (Prod.fst ∘ fun b => (a, b)) :=
                PMF.map_comp _ (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma) Prod.fst
              _ = (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma).map
                  (Function.const gamma a) := by rfl
              _ = PMF.pure a :=
                PMF.map_const (PMF.uniformOfFintype gamma) a
          _ = PMF.uniformOfFintype beta :=
            PMF.bind_pure (PMF.uniformOfFintype beta)
      _ = (uniformDistribution beta).toPMF
          (uniformDistribution_isProbability beta) :=
        (uniformDistribution_toPMF beta).symm

  subst n

noncomputable def seedFiberEquiv (L : LdParams) :
    ScalarQ L ≃ Fin L.m × Fin (L.q / L.m) :=
  (binaryRepresentation L.model).trans <|
    (Equiv.cast <| congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq).trans
      finProdFinEquiv.symm

@[simp] theorem seedFiberEquiv_fst (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) :
    (seedFiberEquiv L s).1 = chiIndex L s := by
  letI : NeZero L.m := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm)⟩

    apply (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul L.seedFiberCard_pos).mpr
    rw [Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd]
    exact (binaryRepresentation L.model s).isLt
  simp only [seedFiberEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply]
  apply Fin.ext
  change
    (Equiv.cast (congrArg Fin L.seedFiberProduct_eq)
      (binaryRepresentation L.model s)).val / (L.q / L.m) =
      (Fin.ofNat L.m ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m))).val
  rw [equivCastFin_val]
  · exact (Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hquot).symm
  · exact L.seedFiberProduct_eq

+The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the

+/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
+weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
+`Distribution`. -/
+theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
+    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
+    μ = ν := by
+  cases μ with
+  | mk s w hn ho =>
+    cases ν with
+    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
+      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
+      have hw : w = w' := hweight
+      subst hs
+      subst hw
+      rfl

+/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
+theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]

+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_

+    rfl
+  · funext c
+    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,

+      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean:327` — `ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL` proves only raw sampler equality, so it cannot discharge `lem:ld-question-typed-cl`’s typed-family claim.
- [ ] F2 (blocker) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:395` — The new Pauli typed-CL node targets an equality-only theorem with an untracked `sorry`, leaving the source conditional-linearity assertion without a faithful Lean target.
- [ ] F3 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistributionAux.lean:203` — The new push-forward API duplicates the extensionality, map-composition, and uniform-marginal infrastructure already in `DistributionMarginals.lean`.
- [ ] F4 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean:117` — `card_chiIndex_fiber` duplicates the existing exact seed-fiber decomposition in `Transport/Correspondence.lean`.

## Review

F1 is source-statement drift. `references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-62` defines a typed family by requiring every member to be conditionally linear, and lines 84-92 define typed CL distributions only from such families. The low-degree construction explicitly gives levels 1, 2, and 3 in `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:203-237`. Nevertheless, `ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL` only proves equality to `typedCLDistribution`, whose signature accepts arbitrary maps. It proves no `IsTypedCondLinearFamily` fact, does not use the newly proved level results, and there is no point-map or common-level family theorem. Thus the `\leanok` at `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:87` is unsupported. Prove the point case, lift all three maps to a common level such as 3, and expose that certification in the linked theorem or alongside the equality; remove `\leanok` until then.

F2 concerns `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1084-1108,1115-1120`, which both assigns CL levels to every Pauli map and concludes that the question law is typed CL. The linked `pauliQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL` at `Test/Completeness.lean:28-33` states only equality and ends in a bare `sorry`. The closer family obligation, `isCondLinear_pauliCL` at `Test/PauliBasisTest.lean:259-261`, also remains a bare `sorry`. Neither cites a tracking issue or paper-gap note. The absent `\leanok` correctly avoids claiming completion, but the new source node still needs a source-faithful open target and explicit proof-debt tracking.

For F3, the stronger `Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight` and `Distribution.map_map` overlap `distribution_eq_of_support_eq_of_toPMF_eq` and `distribution_map_map_of_isProbability`; the new uniform equivalence/projection results also overlap `uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv`. Consolidate these into one lower-level distribution API and migrate both consumer branches.

For F4, `Correspondence.lean:217-276` already constructs `seedFiberEquiv : ScalarQ L ≃ Fin L.m × Fin (L.q / L.m)` and proves its first coordinate is `chiIndex`. Move that decomposition to a lower shared module and derive uniformity from it instead of maintaining a second, lengthy fiber-count calculation.

The line-equivalence, canonical-representative, conditional-linearity-level, and line-sampling statements otherwise agree with the cited paper passages. Earlier module-placement, citation, and line-incidence concerns are resolved. Exact-head local CI is reported green; the worktree and `git diff --check` are clean. The remaining `exists_ld_soundness` proof hole is explicitly documented and tracked by issue #16.
